title: Chapter 11 — Columbiformes
description: Plump, round-headed birds with small bills and a rapid, direct flight. Columbiformes are among the most successful bird orders, inhabiting every continent except Antarctica. They feed on seeds and fruit, drink by sucking water rather than tilting the head back, and produce crop milk to feed their young — a trait otherwise found only in flamingos and some penguins.

children.description: The common bronzewing is a species of medium-sized, heavily built pigeon. Its advertising call is an extraordinary mournful whooo repeated at metronomic intervals.

children.description: The mourning dove is a member of the dove family, Columbidae. The bird is also known as the American mourning dove, the rain dove, and colloquially as the turtle dove, and it was once known as the Carolina pigeon and Carolina turtledove. It is one of the most abundant and widespread North American birds and a popular gamebird, with more than 20 million birds shot annually in the U.S., both for sport and meat.

children.name: Columba livia

children.name: Columba oenas
children.description: The stock dove is a species of bird in the family Columbidae, the doves and pigeons. It is widely distributed in the western Palearctic, north to central Scandinavia and south to northwest Africa. Western and southern populations are resident, while northeastern populations are migratory to avoid the colder winters there.

children.name: Columba oliviae

children.name: Columba palumbus
children.description: The common wood pigeon, also known simply as the wood pigeon, is a large pigeon native to the western Palearctic. It belongs to the genus Columba, which includes closely related species such as the rock dove. It has a flexible diet, feeding mainly on plant material, including cereals, and is therefore considered an agricultural pest.

children.name: Columba rupestris

children.name: Streptopelia orientalis

The species has a wide native distribution range from Central Asia east across Asia to Japan. The populations show variations in the patterning of plumage and have been designated into at least six named subspecies.
